Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

able adjective

be able to

also be able to, can, unable, not able to, be able, could, couldn’t, can’t, cannot, capable, capable of, incapable of

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.34: hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?
Cic. Amic. 62
Traupman 267
Traupman 286

possum, posse, potuī

verb, irregular, with an infinitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

be able, can

“Be able to” is a verb in Latin, not an adjective: possum with the infinitive.

Other words

  • queō, quīre, quīvī (quiī), quitum — be able; mostly with a negative, “cannot”

    verb, irregular, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.1.5: nōn queō reliqua scrībere; Traupman 267; Traupman 286 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • nequeō, nequīre, nequīvī (nequiī), nequitum — be unable, cannot

    verb, irregular, with an infinitive · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.96: cum Dēmosthenēs rhō dīcere nequīret (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Cicero himself writes nōn queō in the first person singular (Lewis & Short).

  • valeō, valēre, valuī, valitum — be strong enough to, have the power to

    verb, second conjugation; with an infinitive mostly in poetry and post-Augustan prose · also used · classical · Hor. C. 1.34.12–13: valet īma summīs mūtāre … deus (Lewis & Short); Phaedr. 4.1.10 (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • hoc puerī possunt, virī nōn poterunt?

    children are able to do this, and men won’t be?Cic. Tusc. 2.34

  • caprās et ovēs quot quisque habēret, dīcere posse, amīcōs quot habēret, nōn posse dīcere

    anyone can say how many goats and sheep he has, but not how many friendsCic. Amic. 62

  • nōn queō reliqua scrībere; tanta vīs lacrimārum est

    I can’t write the rest; the tears are too manyCic. Fam. 14.1.5

See also would.
